bluf: The Social Shepherd is a founder led, Bath based social first agency with 74 people across four hubs in 2025, selling creators, paid social and TikTok Shop to beauty, food, fashion, toy and pet brands. It leads with the award: UK Social Media Agency of the Year in 2025 after two straight Best Large Social Media Agency wins. The record shows a US push (a 2023 expansion, 2026-04-01 blog posts on US city agency lists) and no AI service offer. What a rival should know: the sitemap shows nothing updated in 90 days, it runs no LinkedIn ads while selling paid social, and the record lists no pricing model.
doing:
The positioning line reads: social first agency with UK and US offices linking consumers and brands via content, creators and commerce, pitching playful creative with commercial power. In plain words, a social shop that wants to be judged on sales. The headline claim is an award, UK Social Media Agency of the Year in 2025 after two straight Best Large Social Media Agency wins.

The sold mix is narrow, breadth 4. Creator & Influencer leads at score 3: the site title calls it a global social media agency and its Social and Influencer lines carry the Bio-Oil, Lumene and BARK cases. Paid Social scores 2 on its paid page, with the Passenger case claiming 10x revenue from paid social and search. Retail Media scores 2 because TikTok Shop is a main navigation service: shop and product strategy, creator affiliates, paid ads and content. Paid Search scores 1; SEO, web, data, CRM, programmatic, B2B and AI all score 0. The service list adds social listening, community management and media buying. No proprietary product or partner is listed.

AI posture: no AI service offer; AI appears only in blog and podcast content such as ChatGPT statistics and ChatGPT shopping, alongside its Have You Herd? podcast.

Dated moves: 2023, Best Large Social Media Agency at the UK Social Media Awards (repeated in 2024) and a US expansion announced with planned New York and Miami offices; 2024, a London hub opened, the co founders took CEO and MD roles and the team reached 72; 2025, Sarah took over as MD, co founder Jack moved to CCO, and it won UK Social Media Agency of the Year. The latest dated client case is BARK, 2025-12-26; four service case pages are dated 2026-02-12.

Pricing signals are absent. For a social agency of this size the record also shows no jobs, no ATS, no measurement line, no owned audience line and no AI search capability.
clients:
The client type on record is mixed, across beauty and skincare, food and beverage, fashion and apparel, toys and games and pet; the home market is the UK with hubs in Bath and London, and New York and Miami on the US side.

The record names 10 clients: 7 observed and 3 names only. Beyblade (case dated 2023-02-24), Bio-Oil (2023-04-21), Lumene (2023-04-21), Passenger (2024-01-05) and BARK (2025-12-26) each carry a case study read as social and creators, brand and creative and organic demand; the excerpts captured only navigation text, so what each came for rests on the titles and the capability notes, which credit the Passenger case with a claim of 10x revenue from paid social and search and place Bio-Oil, Lumene and BARK on the Social and Influencer lines. Charlotte Tilbury and Mia Tui are logos on the influencer services page, read as social and creators from that slug. Lavazza, Lounge by Zalando and Arla are homepage logos with no described work; their needs are inferred from the creator, paid social and TikTok Shop mix it leads with. One shared client: Lavazza also sits on the book of webranking.

The observed mix is social and creators (share 0.545), brand and creative (0.273) and organic demand (0.182). What this base needs next, hedged: consumer brands buying creators are the ones KJ8 (Human provenance becomes a distribution signal) favours, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that they keep buying creator work here; the paid social hours sit under KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out) and KJ5 (The price of attention splits in two), so there is a roughly even chance those clients ask next for the measurement and first party data the record does not show it selling.
house: Say and do: 2 of 3 tested lines are practised on its own house. Paid Social is corroborated: meta_pixel and linkedin_insight run on its own site. Creator & Influencer is corroborated: its own short form channels, Instagram and YouTube, are linked from the site. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: it sells paid social and the Ad Library shows 0 ads. The Transparency Center shows 1 Google ad, from The Social Shepherd Ltd, last shown 2026-06-09, 0 in the last 30 days. The tag stack is GTM with the two pixels on Craft CMS; no test tool or ABM stack was detected. Content velocity: the sitemap lists 299 URLs, 266 updated in 365 days and 0 in 90 days, so publishing has gone quiet since the 2026-04-01 run of US city agency list posts. It publishes no llms.txt, blocks no AI crawlers, and 3 AI topic URLs sit in the sitemap. No Meta or TikTok ad library reading is on record.
market:
Horus reads The Social Shepherd at a tailwind index of 4.6, band Neutral, 28th percentile. It is best placed for KJ8, human provenance becoming a distribution signal, driven by Creator & Influencer at +2. It is most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle being hollowed out (Paid Social and Paid Search at -1 each). Best scenario fit is The Commons Rebuilt at 50/100. It is making P4; partial on P2 (some feed or entity work, not a named line); absent on P1, P6, P7 and P8; P5 unknown; P3 not applicable.

Monsoon reads 37.3, band Doldrums, 6th percentile: migration 38.3 against displacement 36.3, the read classed observed. The verdict puts 33 of the index on the sold mix, Paid Social and Retail Media carrying the most movable hours, with automation overlapping 50% of them; the shore split is 65% South and Southeast Asia, 20% Eastern Europe, 15% Africa and the Maghreb. openings:
The strongest opening is the idle publishing machine behind a social first pitch: the sitemap shows 0 URLs updated in 90 days, the last dated run being the 2026-04-01 US city agency list posts. A rival that shows a live weekly cadence and a creator provenance product is likely, with moderate confidence, to win a beauty or food brand review against it. The falsifier: a fresh run of dated posts and case studies in the next compile.

The contradiction to lead with is LinkedIn: it sells paid social and the Ad Library shows 0 ads of its own. The gap to lead with is measurement: data and measurement, CRM and AI all score 0, so its paid social hours sit exposed under KJ6 with no first party data or measurement depth in the record to defend them. A rival that prices on outcomes undercuts an agency whose record lists no pricing model (P5 unknown).

Contestable clients: 3 of its 10 clients are names only (Lavazza, Lounge by Zalando, Arla), and Lavazza also sits with webranking. The Monsoon displacement of 36.3 means an offshore rate undercut is unlikely to move this book; the contest is on cadence, provenance and proof.
